CanvasBackground.description: Solid canonical uppercase #RRGGBBAA, or a top-to-bottom linear gradient.

LinearGradientBackground.description: Top-to-bottom linear gradient. There is no angle field. stops has 2 through 8 entries, strictly increasing at in [0, 1], first at=0, last at=1.

LinearGradientStop.description: One stop on a top-to-bottom linear canvas background. at=0 is the top edge, at=1 is the bottom edge.

MediaSelectorWeights.description: Shares of a weighted selector, keyed by media id or tag:NAME. An item's weight is its media id key if present; otherwise the first tag:NAME key, in alphabetical order, among the tags it carries, with that weight split equally among the items of the selection that share the key, so a sponsor's share holds however many creatives it has; otherwise the item is its own group with weight 1. Every full cycle plays each item exactly its share.

PageDataCondition.description: A card-data predicate, evaluated before civil time. Missing or expired data never matches. The page also respects its ordinary time bounds. Requires host capability page.conditions; older hosts receive the page disabled.

equals.description: Optional scalar equality. Omitting it tests existence, including a present null or false.

key.description: Project card data key or card instance ID; feed keys are not accepted. The key {screen.weather} reads the weather conditions of each screen's own location: the document has condition (clear, cloud, fog, rain, snow, storm or wind), band (freezing below 0 degrees Celsius, cold 0 to 9, mild 10 to 17, warm 18 to 24, hot from 25), temperatureC (whole degrees) and isDay. Point path at one of them, for example path /condition with equals rain. The condition is the current observation for the screen's 0.25 degree cell, about hourly, not a forecast. A screen without a location never matches.

path.description: RFC 6901 pointer with at most 16 segments; absent or empty tests the document itself.

PageVisibility.description: Optional page visibility schedule. It is a sibling of advance and is never part of screenrig.canvas/v1; it describes playback orchestration, not geometry. The server validates and carries these rules as data. The player evaluates them against the screen timezone published at the manifest root. A page is eligible when enabled is true, now is inside [from, until), and either windows is absent or at least one window matches. Every playlist must keep at least one page with no visibility field at all, so eligible content always exists. Conformance vectors for the evaluation rules are the screenrig.schedule/v1 family in packages/schedule-contract.

enabled.description: False hides the page unconditionally and needs no clock. A visibility object that sets enabled true and carries no from, until, windows or data is a no-op and is rejected.

from.description: Inclusive civil lower bound in the screen timezone, minute precision, no offset and no zone suffix.

until.description: Exclusive civil upper bound in the screen timezone. When both bounds are present, from must be strictly earlier than until.

PageVisibilityWindow.description: One recurring civil window. Omitting start and end selects the whole day. When end is less than or equal to start the window crosses midnight and the start day owns it, so fri 22:00 to 02:00 runs into Saturday morning.

days.description: Civil days of week. The server stores them in mon-to-sun order; the set carries no author-visible ordering.

end.description: Exclusive civil end time. Required when start is present.

start.description: Inclusive civil start time. Required when end is present.

application_id.description: Optional ownership assertion; the server resolves the authoritative application from release_id.

rect.description: Required unless displays is set. With displays, omit it or send the rect derived from them.

PlaylistAudioCue.description: Optional soundtrack hint on an ordinary page. When the page becomes current, the Player switches to the named track from its start unless it is already playing; restart true restarts it even then. The sequence continues from that track. Players may ignore a hint. track must name a track id in the playlist audio; a cue without a playlist audio is invalid_request. Not allowed on adslot pages. A page with advance mode audio_end ends when the cued track ends; it requires this cue.

PlaylistAudioEndAdvanceWrite.description: The page ends when the soundtrack track its audio_cue names ends. The page must carry an audio_cue and the playlist an audio soundtrack (docs/playlist-audio.md).

max_ms.description: Optional client safety hint; the server resolves the authoritative deadline from the cued track's verified duration.

id.description: Playlist-unique track id that page audio_cue hints name.

media_id.description: An owned, ready audio media object.

PlaylistAudioWrite.description: Optional playlist soundtrack: ordered ready audio (MP3) media that plays continuously while pages change (docs/playlist-audio.md). Page changes never stop or restart it. PUT replaces the whole playlist, so omitting audio removes the soundtrack.

cued.description: true stops the soundtrack after each track: a track plays only when a page audio_cue starts it, so each page and its track stay bound. false plays the tracks back to back.

loop.description: After the last track, start again at the first. false stops after the last track. Ignored when cued is true.

tracks.description: Play order. Track ids are unique within the playlist; the same media may appear under two ids.

volume.description: Soundtrack gain, multiplied by the Player's own volume.

PlaylistCardPrimitiveWrite.description: A built-in card the Player draws natively (clock, weather, menu board, ticker, KPI tiles and the rest of the vendored cards catalog, screenrig.cards.contract/v1). layout places it: full (the whole canvas), free (your own rect and layer), center (900 x 420), wide (the canvas inset 30 from the left and right and 80 from the top and bottom), header (the whole top edge, 80 high), footer (the whole bottom edge, 80 high), corner (270 square), chip (240 x 70) or strip (the whole edge, 120 high), in 1080p design units scaled by min(canvas width, canvas height) / 1080. corner and chip take an anchor corner (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) and strip an anchor edge (top, bottom, left, right); the other layouts take none. Except for free, the server derives rect and layer from the canvas, or from the frame displays cover: omit them, or send exactly what it derives. A page holds at most one full, center or wide card, one corner or chip card per corner, and one strip per edge (a card with presence may share an edge with a normal strip); a header takes the top edge's normal strip slot and a footer the bottom edge's, so a page holds at most one of each, no normal strip on that edge, and a card with presence may still share it. A corner or chip on an edge that holds a strip moves in past it by 120, and past a header or footer by 80. On a playlist with a format, displays is the frame the layout derives in (full is the frame, corner the frame's corner; free refuses displays), the card scale is the tile's min(width, height) / 1080 = 1 rather than derived from the frame, and two cards compete for a slot, or move in past each other's strips, only when their frames share a display (no displays is every display). A card's tier decides its layouts (GET /api/card-types): core takes all nine, fullscreen takes full. params holds the placement's static properties (theme, location, titles, column definitions) and changes only with a republish. A string in params may carry {screen.name}, {screen.timezone} and {screen.field.NAME}, and a location param may be the string {screen.location}; the backend expands them for each screen, so one playlist shows every screen its own values. data names a card data document (GET/PUT /api/card-data/{key}) that holds the card's dynamic properties (menu sections, ticker items, KPI tiles); agents change it without a republish. {screen.field.NAME} in a data key reads a per-screen document, for example menu-{screen.field.store_number}. With data, params may not carry dynamic properties; without it, params carry the whole configuration. Every string in params that begins with media: is a media reference, media:<id>, naming a ready image in this project that the card draws (spotlight people[].photo, product-grid products[].photo); a card never takes an image URL. Publish refuses an unknown card or major and invalid params (card_invalid), a layout, anchor, rect or layer the card may not carry (card_layout_invalid), cards that claim one place on the page (card_layout_conflict), a media reference that names no ready image of the project (card_media_invalid), and a bound key whose stored document the card rejects (card_data_invalid). The screens showing the placement are granted its media, and a live write approves pending media it names, as with a by:id selector. A card with a third-party feed (weather) reads it from the key the server derives from its static params.

anchor.description: Required for corner and chip (a corner) and strip (an edge); not allowed for full, free, center, wide, header and footer.

card.description: Global crd_ UID. Inline catalogue type, major, params and data are deprecated for one release and converted on publish.

data.description: Card data key holding the dynamic properties. May not start with feed:. {screen.field.NAME} in the key reads a per-screen document, for example menu-{screen.field.store_number}: the backend fills in each screen's own field.

displays.description: Playlists with a format only. The displays whose frame the layout derives in: full is the frame, corner the frame's corner, and so on. Ascending unique 1-based display numbers within 1..format.displays that fill a rectangle of the wall's tiles, such as [2] or [1, 2]. Absent is every display. Not allowed for layout free.

layer.description: Required for layout free. Fixed for every other layout (full 10, center and wide 20, strip, header and footer 30, corner 40, chip 50): omit it or send that value.

major.description: Card major version. Absent selects the catalog's current major, which the stored placement then pins.

params.description: Static params, validated against the card's params schema. A string that begins with media: is a media reference, media:<id>. A string may carry {screen.name}, {screen.timezone} and {screen.field.NAME}, and a location param may be the string {screen.location}; the backend expands them for each screen.

rect.description: Required for layout free. For every other layout omit it or send the rect the server derives; left and right strips are the band on that edge (120 units wide, canvas high), which the Player draws as a horizontal strip turned 90 degrees.

PlaylistDisplays.description: Playlists with a format only. The displays a primitive covers: ascending unique 1-based display numbers within 1..format.displays that fill a rectangle of the wall's tiles, such as [2], [1, 2] or, on a grid of 4 columns, [2, 3, 6, 7]. In a row or a column they are contiguous. The server derives rect as the bounding box of those tiles; rect is omitted or exactly the derived value. Stored and echoed on read.

until.description: The page lasts until its YouTube video ends. The page must hold exactly one YouTube video (a link to one video, not a YouTube playlist or live stream); a page that does not is refused at advance.until. after_ms is then how long the page shows when the screen cannot read the video's length.

PlaylistFormat.description: The video wall a playlist is authored for: 2 to 12 displays, tiles of 1920 x 1080 (landscape) or 1080 x 1920 (portrait), laid out in a row, a column or a grid. A row has the displays as columns and one row, a column one column and the displays as rows, a grid columns and displays / columns rows. Display n sits at column (n - 1) mod columns and row floor((n - 1) / columns): left to right, then top to bottom. The canvas of c columns and r rows of tiles of width w and height h is (c * w, r * h), for example 5760 x 1080 for 3 landscape displays in a row, 1080 x 3840 for 2 portrait displays in a column and 7680 x 3240 for 12 landscape displays in a grid of 4 columns. Every ordinary page's canvas width and height must equal it exactly, else 400 invalid_request at pages[i].canvas. Card scale on such a playlist is the tile's min(width, height) / 1080 = 1. A playlist with a format may be bound only to a screen whose wall has the same shape (displays = number of outputs, arrangement, columns, portrait if and only if rotation is 90 or 270), else 409 playlist_format_mismatch: assignment, fleet assignment, schedule entries and takeover. A playlist without a format binds to any screen.

columns.description: Displays per row of a grid. Required for arrangement grid and not allowed otherwise; displays divided by columns is at least 2. Echoed for a grid only.

fallback_src.description: The page a screen shows in src's place when src does not load: a network, DNS, TLS or connection error, an HTTP status of 400 or above, or no completed load within 30 seconds. Takes the forms and rules of src (a pasted iframe embed code, a YouTube link stored as its canonical embed, a Google or Microsoft document link stored rebuilt for the screen, with the document_not_shared refusal). Omit it for none; an empty string is refused.

navigation_allowlist.description: Where the page may navigate, as 1 to 64 entries. Each entry is [scheme://]host[:port][path], a CSP host-source: the scheme is http or https (an http entry also matches https; no scheme matches both); host is a name, an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address in brackets, *.name (any subdomain of name, not name itself) or *, with no other wildcard; port is a number or * (absent: the scheme's default port); a path ending in / or /* covers everything under it, any other path only itself. No credentials, query, fragment, spaces or ; , ' " characters. With a list, the page's own links, scripted navigations, forms and redirects reach only src, fallback_src and addresses an entry matches; a refused navigation leaves the page where it was. Query and fragment never count, and a redirect is matched without its path. Frames inside the page and YouTube embeds are not restricted. Entries are stored with the scheme and host lowercased and /* written as /, repeats removed. An empty array is refused: omit the key for no restriction.

rect.description: Required unless displays is set. With displays, omit it or send the rect derived from them.

reload_s.description: Seconds between reloads of the page while it is on glass: 0 (no reload, the default) or 60 to 86400. Each reload loads src again, so a recovered src replaces the fallback. A write of 0 stores nothing.

src.description: An http or https page, any host including the screen's LAN, with optional user:pass@ credentials, or a pasted iframe embed code, read for its src. Native Players show all of these; the web Player only https pages without credentials. A Google Slides, Docs or Sheets link or a Microsoft 365 Embed link is stored rebuilt for the screen; a file that asks viewers to sign in is refused (document_not_shared).

dwell_ms.description: Required on media_end image primitives. Forbidden on duration and application pages.

rect.description: Required unless displays is set. With displays, omit it or send the rect derived from them.

max_ms.description: Optional client safety hint; the server resolves the authoritative deadline from resolved item lengths.

batch_size.description: Maximum media per visit; omitted plays the remaining pass. one_at_a_time requires 1.

fit.description: aspect keeps only media whose width over height is within 5% of the primitive's rect, so a portrait slot never plays a landscape file. Read when the selector resolves, from the stored rect (a video wall or display frame included); the Player is unchanged.

order.description: filename plays the pass in filename order, random shuffles each pass, weighted rotates by weights: one item per visit, so one_at_a_time or batch_size 1 is required.

PlaylistMediaSelectorByFolder.description: The ready files of the primitive directly inside one media folder (GET /api/media-folders), not those of its subfolders, ordered and paced like by:all. Like a tag, the folder is read again at every selector resolve, so moving files in or out changes what playing screens show from their next loop. Writing a playlist requires the folder to exist in the project; it may be empty. A folder that holds no ready file of the primitive, or is deleted later, matches nothing. Players receive it as by:all; the server resolves the folder.

batch_size.description: Maximum media per visit; omitted plays the remaining pass. one_at_a_time requires 1.

fit.description: aspect keeps only media whose width over height is within 5% of the primitive's rect, so a portrait slot never plays a landscape file. Read when the selector resolves, from the stored rect (a video wall or display frame included); the Player is unchanged.

order.description: filename plays the pass in filename order, random shuffles each pass, weighted rotates by weights: one item per visit, so one_at_a_time or batch_size 1 is required.

batch_size.description: Maximum media per visit; omitted plays the remaining pass. one_at_a_time requires 1.

fit.description: aspect keeps only media whose width over height is within 5% of the primitive's rect, so a portrait slot never plays a landscape file. Read when the selector resolves, from the stored rect (a video wall or display frame included); the Player is unchanged.

order.description: filename plays the pass in filename order, random shuffles each pass, weighted rotates by weights: one item per visit, so one_at_a_time or batch_size 1 is required.

tag.description: A tag, or a template with {screen.id} (the screen's identifier without its scr_ prefix) or {screen.field.NAME}, filled for each screen when the selector resolves, so one playlist plays each screen's own media. Filled, it follows the tag rules; a screen without the field, or with a value that is not a tag, selects nothing and the manifest carries screen_fact_missing or screen_fact_invalid.

PlaylistPrimitiveLocked.description: A locked primitive is fixed brand content of a template (logo, background, layout, theme): only the project owner or a member who can approve adds, removes, moves or edits it, or clears its lock, and a playlist made from the template keeps it locked. Omitted means unlocked. A locked primitive cannot read a field. A write by anyone else is primitive_locked (403), or a review under Propose.

PlaylistStinger.description: A transition-only stinger card (major 1). All members are optional; defaults stay in the synthetic runtime placement. hang_ms defaults to 1000 and is at most 60% of the transition duration_ms (checked by the server). logo names a ready image in this project, using the card media grant path.

rect.description: Required unless displays is set. With displays, omit it or send the rect derived from them.

PlaylistTransition.description: Page transition. type and duration_ms are both required; OpenAPI does not default them. Swipe authoring examples use duration_ms 600; that value is not a schema default.

color.description: Dip stage fill; allowed only on dip. Defaults to black.

ease.description: Optional cubic ease; forbidden on stinger. Defaults to linear for crossfade/swipe and in-out for dip/wipe/slide.

rect.description: Required unless displays is set. With displays, omit it or send the rect derived from them.

format.description: Omitted means none: an ordinary playlist.

pages.description: The pages of one playlist may resolve to at most 1024 media references in total. A by:ids selector counts its length; a by:all, by:tag or by:folder definition reserves 32 references independently of catalog size. The actual loop snapshot is bounded at 1024 media references in total. Above either budget is 422 invalid at path pages.

PrimitiveEnter.description: Optional object enter. Playlist write and the runtime manifest use this object as-is; there is no snake_case rename inside it. Absent means paint at rest, full opacity. Optional integer stagger 0 through 8 delays start by stagger*120 ms after the shared 500 ms delay. Absent or 0 is today's start. Duration is a named constant in screenrig.canvas/v1.

stagger.description: Optional per-primitive enter delay in steps of 120 ms after OBJECT_ENTER_DELAY_MS. Absent or 0 is the same start as today.

PrimitiveMotion.description: Optional persistent object motion. Playlist write and the runtime manifest use this object as-is; there is no snake_case rename inside it. Absent means the primitive stays at rest after enter. Copied through uninterpolated. spin and drift apply to image and video only; application and iframe with spin or drift are rejected by the server (motion_not_allowed_for_primitive). path applies to image, video, application, and iframe. This restriction is not encoded as OpenAPI if/then.

PrimitiveMotionDrift.description: Continuous slow scale about the clipRect centre combined with a slow translate. Image and video only; the server rejects drift on application and iframe. Ping-pongs; never jumps.

PrimitiveMotionPath.description: Translation along a polyline of canvas-unit waypoints after the authored rect. loop defaults to loop when omitted. Valid on image, video, application, and iframe.

PrimitiveMotionSpin.description: Continuous rotation about the clipRect centre. Image and video only; the server rejects spin on application and iframe.

url.description: The camera's or recorder's RTSP URL, as it gives it (user:pass@ and LAN hosts included). The Player connects to it directly.

StreamSourceWrite.description: A stream source. A source may give only its url and let the scheme name the protocol: https is hls, rtsp and rtsps are rtsp.

group.description: IPv4 ASM group within 239.0.0.0/8. Raw MPEG-TS over UDP, not RTP.
